title: Challenges to Do at Home: 70 Fun, Safe Ideas to Try
h1: Challenges to Do at Home: 70 Fun, Safe Ideas for Couples, Friends and Family
description: Looking for challenges to do at home? Try 70 fun, safe ideas for couples, friends and family, from food and blindfold games to creative and fitness dares.
excerpt: 70 fun, low-cost challenges to do at home with a partner, friends or family, plus the viral stunts you should skip and how to film them well.
intro:
A rainy Saturday, a quiet date night, a group chat that keeps saying “we should do something” — sometimes the best plan is a silly challenge in your own living room. Challenges give everyone a goal, a little friendly pressure and a guaranteed story to laugh about later. They are also cheap: most of the ideas below use things you already own.

This list collects 70 challenges to do at home, grouped by vibe so you can pick quickly: food and taste tests, blindfold games, couple challenges, creative contests, fitness dares and screen-free classics. We also flag the viral stunts that went too far, so your fun night never ends with a trip to urgent care.
body:
Why challenges to do at home are worth a try

Challenges work because they turn ordinary time together into play. Instead of scrolling side by side, you are competing, cheering and messing up in front of each other, which is exactly how inside jokes are born. For couples, playful novelty is one of the easiest ways to keep things from feeling routine. For friends and families, a challenge gives quieter people an easy way to join in without having to carry a conversation.

  • Low cost: most need snacks, paper, a phone timer or nothing at all.
  • Flexible: play for ten minutes or turn it into a full tournament night.
  • Shareable: many make great short videos if you like posting, but they are just as fun unfilmed.
Tip: Agree on the rules before you start: who judges, how points work and what the loser does. A tiny prize, like picking the next movie, keeps everyone invested.

Food and taste-test challenges

Food challenges are crowd favorites because the reactions are half the fun. Keep portions small and check for allergies first.

  1. Blind taste test: Blindfold a player and have them identify five snacks, sodas or chip flavors.
  2. Guess that pizza: Order or make pizzas with different toppings and guess each one with eyes closed.
  3. Smoothie roulette: Write ingredients on slips of paper, draw three and blend whatever comes up.
  4. Sour candy face-off: Eat a sour candy without making a face. First to wince loses.
  5. Eat it or wear it: Pick a bag at random; you either eat the mystery item or wear it as a hat (use mild foods only).
  6. Cheap vs. expensive: Taste two versions of the same food and guess which is the pricey brand.
  7. Cook-a-meal challenge: Each person gets the same five ingredients and 30 minutes. Everyone judges.
  8. Mystery basket: One person picks pantry items; the other must make a snack using all of them.
  9. Chopsticks challenge: Move jelly beans or cereal from one bowl to another with chopsticks in one minute.
  10. Cookie face: Place a cookie on your forehead and get it to your mouth without using hands.
  11. Mild hot sauce ladder: Try progressively spicier sauces, stopping when you choose. No pressure, no super-hots.
  12. Homemade sundae race: Build the most creative sundae in three minutes.
  13. Gummy vs. real food: Guess whether a candy shaped like food is the real thing or the gummy version.
  14. Silent snack: Eat a crunchy chip without making a sound.

Blindfold and guessing challenges

Blindfolds instantly make everyday tasks hilarious. Clear the floor first and keep a spotter nearby.

  1. Blindfolded makeup: One partner does the other's makeup without looking.
  2. Blindfolded drawing: Draw a portrait of each other while blindfolded, then reveal.
  3. What's in the box: Reach into a box and guess the household object by touch.
  4. Guess the smell: Identify spices, candles or lotions by scent alone.
  5. Blindfolded Lego build: Recreate a simple model with your eyes closed while a partner gives directions.
  6. Human Shazam: Play the first two seconds of a song and race to name it.
  7. Hum that tune: Hum a song with your mouth closed while others guess.
  8. Voice guess: Blindfolded players guess who is speaking in a funny accent.
  9. Blindfolded outfit: Pick an outfit from your partner's closet without looking. They have to wear it for an hour.
  10. Sock sort: Match pairs of socks from a pile while blindfolded against the clock.

Challenges to do at home as a couple

These are designed for two people and work for new couples and long-term partners alike. For conversation-based games, pair them with our would you rather questions for couples.

  1. Who knows who best: Write answers about each other on paper, then compare.
  2. Couple's quiz: Quiz each other on first-date details, favorite foods and childhood stories.
  3. Recreate your first photo: Find your first picture together and recreate it as closely as possible.
  4. Do my hair: One partner styles the other's hair using a tutorial.
  5. Swap routines: Spend an evening doing each other's usual chores and hobbies.
  6. Most likely to: Read out prompts and point at whoever is “most likely to” do it.
  7. 36 questions night: Take turns with deep questions and no phones.
  8. Two-minute portrait: Sketch each other in two minutes, then frame the worst one.
  9. Dance tutorial challenge: Learn a short routine together and film the final take.
  10. Accent challenge: Read words or phrases from a card in different accents and judge each other kindly.
  11. Phone swap: Trade playlists for a night and rate the other's music taste.
  12. Tag questions: Answer a set of “getting to know you” questions on camera, then tag a friend couple.

If you want even more prompts, our get to know me questions slot neatly into a quiz-style challenge night.

Creative and DIY challenges

Creative challenges are calmer but still competitive. They work well for mixed ages and anyone who does not love physical games.

  1. 100 layer challenge: Stack 100 layers of something safe, like nail polish coats, stickers or paper cups.
  2. One-color outfit: Build the best outfit using only one color from your closet.
  3. Ten-dollar art: Create a piece of art using only items you find in a junk drawer.
  4. Story chain: Each person adds one sentence to a story; anyone who laughs is out.
  5. Mannequin challenge: Freeze in a dramatic scene while someone films a slow walk-through.
  6. Lip-sync battle: Pick songs out of a hat and perform them with full commitment.
  7. Rebrand a cereal: Design a new box and slogan for a cereal in 15 minutes.
  8. Fort-building contest: Build a blanket fort; best engineering and coziest interior win.
  9. Paper airplane distance: Fold, fly and measure. Three attempts each.
  10. Haiku duel: Write a haiku about a random household object.
  11. Recreate a famous painting: Use props from around the house and take a photo.
  12. Rhyme time: Speak only in rhymes for five minutes.
  13. Room makeover sprint: Restyle one shelf or corner in 20 minutes using what you have.
  14. Movie in emojis: Text a movie plot using only emojis and race to guess.

Fitness and coordination challenges

Get moving without a gym. Warm up, skip anything that hurts and keep breakables out of range.

  1. Plank-off: Who can hold a plank longest?
  2. Wall sit showdown: Same idea, with legs burning.
  3. Balloon keep-up: Keep a balloon in the air without letting it touch the floor.
  4. Toilet paper toss: Land rolls in a laundry basket from increasing distances.
  5. Bottle flip: First person to land five flips wins.
  6. Cup stacking speed run: Build and collapse a pyramid of plastic cups as fast as possible.
  7. Sock toss crossbar: Hang a string across a doorway and try to arc rolled socks over it.
  8. One-legged chores: Do the dishes balancing on one foot.
  9. Partner yoga: Copy beginner partner poses from a video.
  10. Hula hoop marathon: Longest spin wins.
  11. Push-up ladder: Add one push-up per round until someone taps out.
  12. Dance freeze: Dance until the music stops; anyone who moves is out.

Quick, screen-free classics

Perfect for a group, a family dinner or a power outage. Many of these overlap with our favorite challenges to do with friends.

  1. 7-second challenge: Name three things in a category within seven seconds.
  2. Try not to laugh: Take turns telling bad jokes to a stone-faced opponent.
  3. Whisper challenge: One person wears headphones and lip-reads a phrase.
  4. Alphabet categories: Name an animal, food or city for every letter in order.
  5. Don't say “um”: Talk about a random topic for one minute with no filler words.
  6. Ice bucket (gentle edition): A splash of cool water outdoors for a cause you care about, never ice-cold dunking.
  7. Cotton ball scoop: Move cotton balls between bowls using a spoon held in your mouth.
  8. Truth-or-dare lightning round: Fast questions only; skip any dare someone is not comfortable with. Need ideas? Try our truth or dare questions for adults.

Viral challenges you should skip

Some famous internet challenges caused real injuries, so they are not included above. Skip these, even if a friend insists:

  • Cinnamon challenge: swallowing dry cinnamon can be inhaled into the lungs.
  • Salt and ice challenge: it can cause burn-like skin injuries.
  • Chubby bunny: stuffing marshmallows into your mouth is a choking hazard.
  • Drinking or chugging challenges: speed-drinking alcohol, milk or water can make people seriously ill.
  • Extreme pepper challenges: super-hot peppers have sent people to the ER.
  • Cold tub and dizzy challenges: cold shock and falls are real risks.
  • Anything involving swallowing non-food items or harming another person, including “human dartboard” style stunts.
Tip: A good rule: if a challenge only works because it is a little dangerous, swap it for a version that is funny instead. Laughter is the point, not pain.

How to make your challenge night a hit

  1. Pick a theme. Food night, couples night or a tournament with five mixed rounds.
  2. Set a scoreboard. A whiteboard or notes app keeps things competitive.
  3. Respect “pass.” Everyone can skip any challenge, no questions asked.
  4. Film with permission. Ask before posting anyone's video, especially kids or shy guests.
  5. End with something cozy. Snacks, a movie or a low-key chat helps the night land softly.

Want to turn this into a date? Pick three challenges, add takeout and you have a cheap, memorable evening. For more ideas tailored to personality, browse our date ideas for each zodiac sign.
takeaways: The best challenges to do at home need only snacks, paper, a timer or a blindfold.
Group challenges by vibe — food, blindfold, couple, creative, fitness — to plan an easy night.
Skip viral stunts with real injury risks, such as the cinnamon, salt-and-ice and chubby bunny challenges.
Agree on rules, let anyone pass and ask before posting videos of other people.

faq.q: What are some fun challenges to do at home with no supplies?
faq.a: The 7-second challenge, try not to laugh, alphabet categories, story chain, dance freeze, plank-offs and the don't-say-um challenge all need nothing but people and a phone timer. They are easy to start on the spot and work for couples, friends or families of any size.

faq.q: What challenges can couples do at home?
faq.a: Couples can try who-knows-who-best quizzes, recreating their first photo, blindfolded makeup or drawing, swapping playlists, learning a dance routine or a cook-off with the same five ingredients. Choose playful challenges that get you laughing together rather than ones that embarrass either partner.

faq.q: Are viral TikTok challenges safe to do at home?
faq.a: Many are harmless, but some have caused real injuries, including the cinnamon, salt-and-ice, chubby bunny and extreme pepper challenges. Before trying any trend, ask whether it involves choking, burns, falls, excess alcohol or swallowing non-food items. If it does, skip it or make a safe version.

faq.q: How do you make a challenge night more fun?
faq.a: Pick a theme, keep score, set a small prize like choosing the next movie, and mix short active rounds with calmer creative ones. Let anyone pass without pressure, and only film or post with everyone's permission. Finish with snacks or a movie so the night ends relaxed.
